defaults.permitted_development: Across Oxfordshire, detached domestic garages are usually easiest on the planning permission route when they stay clearly secondary to the house, respect height and boundary relationships, and avoid creating a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. The planning route is usually strongest when the garage looks like a subordinate domestic building rather than a second focal point on the plot.

rules.height_rules: Garage proposals across Oxfordshire are normally judged first on overall height, eaves height and whether the roof form keeps the building subordinate to the main house.
rules.depth_rules: Across Oxfordshire, garage depth and footprint are usually most straightforward when the building sits in a logical side or rear position and leaves enough garden and turning space around it. Very deep or bulky garages can stop feeling incidental even if the height looks modest.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour relationship and vehicle access are the recurring pressure points for garages in Oxfordshire, especially where a new crossover or tight turning arrangement is involved.
rules.roof_rules: Low-profile garage roofs are generally easier than taller roof forms that create storage volume, apparent accommodation or a more dominant outbuilding shape.
rules.materials_rules: Garages are normally easiest to support when the materials, door treatment and overall appearance sit comfortably with the house and local street scene.

rules.permitted_development: In Cherwell, a detached garage is usually easiest to keep off the formal planning permission route when it remains clearly secondary to the house, sits comfortably within the plot and does not create a more dominant frontage or access arrangement. Schemes are usually safer where the roof stays low and the access arrangement still feels practical and visually calm from the road.

rules.height_rules: In Cherwell, garage height is usually the first measurement to sense-check, especially where the building sits close to a boundary or uses a taller pitched roof.
rules.depth_rules: A garage in Cherwell is more likely to need a closer review if the footprint starts to dominate the garden or front part of the site rather than sitting as a modest supporting structure.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary siting, neighbour impact and highway practicality all matter in Cherwell, particularly if the garage depends on a new or altered vehicle access.
rules.roof_rules: Garage roofs in Cherwell are usually easiest where they stay low-profile and do not suggest loft storage, accommodation or a second-storey form.
rules.materials_rules: Materials and frontage treatment should help the garage read as a subordinate domestic building in Cherwell, not as a visually dominant addition to the property.

restrictions.conservation_area: Garages in conservation areas within Cherwell often receive a closer design review where they affect the character of a visible frontage or the wider street scene.
restrictions.listed_building: Garages affecting a listed building or its setting in Cherwell usually need a more careful planning and heritage consent check.
